results.summary: Grounding done. Inventory of 18 capabilities: 12 built (the grade ladder, the smelter, power cell and emanator lines, study-the-wreck, the Ancient Component, the hidden donor smelter, Mod Settings, wrecks drawing pipes, and three riders: alloy forge gates, the one salvage rule, the distillation module) and 6 not built (a wreck found in the world, a source of Ancient Components, wealth exclusion, the grade-changed signal, turrets, more factory machines). Nothing was ever played live beyond one build-over on 2026-09-01 and def loads. Feasibility settled from the game source and the neighbours: the base game has a study-in-place mechanism that needs no other mod, and three placement routes for wrecks already work in this repo. His design-session words of 2026-08-12 to 2026-09-20 had no ledger event; 12 are now recorded on the item and cited. Five draft asks wait for stages 1-2 (a look at what is built, the root, how a wreck is found, how study feels, the three riders). Ten contradictions recorded, four core. Three helpers (Explore, sonnet) charged.

quick_look.scene: One save on the mod's small list: the smelter at all four grades side by side, the power cell and the psychic emanator at three grades each, a wreck with a colonist sent to study it (Research Reinvented is on the list), and a kludged smelter half-built over a wreck. He sees whether the grades can be told apart by eye, whether a grade built over the last reads as a repair or as a build menu, and what study at a wreck looks like today. A sitting with him, or an agent's walk that brings him zoomed captures; the Conductor stages it.

results.summary: Turn 1 sent (design/concepts/WreckedMachines/turn_01.md). It offers a look at the running mod first, writes the case for and against a generic version, and puts a root paragraph before him: ancient machines that no colony can make, found broken, studied at the machine itself, rebuilt in place grade over grade, never equal to the original. Three asks sent, all passed by a fresh Opus judge (a467e768ff82de4be) and narrowed on its review: a_root (is the paragraph the mod; the doubted word is 'any' in 'any RimWorld game', because the mod does not load without the factory mod), a_how_found (a wreck only in ancient-ruin rooms, or also now and then on an ordinary map; recommended: also on an ordinary map), a_riders (the alloy forge steps, the salvage rule and the distillation machine: outside the promise and working as today, or bars of their own; recommended: outside). Held for stage 2: how study feels (after the look), where an Ancient Component comes from, wealth. New core contradiction c_factory_mod_required.

Stage 1 done: the root is his own statement. He answered all three asks of turn 1 (OWNER:1795755622961436106, 1795755647483442186, 1795755673273656447); all three are cited in record.json and written word for word in log.md. a_root: he typed his statement of the mod and allowed a rephrasing; record.json root holds his words, the rephrased text and each wording that is not his. The mod changes specified machines that install like furniture into ancient machines that a colony can no longer research and build; a colony finds one, brings it to a safe place, studies it to open its research, and repairs it through Wrecked (does not work), Kludged (minimal) and Refurbished (full function, slower); the Original is for comparison only; each repair needs study, bench time and resources, and the last needs a rare Ancient Component; 0.1.0 supports only the factory mod and some vanilla items (power supply, psychic emitter). a_how_found: ruins, plus a rare wreck on an ordinary map (by card). a_riders: he called the ask confounded and answered per thing: the forge's order is the Utinni tier's decision, the distillation machine is FlowWorks'; the Designer's call d_riders_fate puts all three rules outside 0.1.0's bars (the salvage rule on the Designer's own call, since he did not speak of it). A lesson is filed on the confounded ask. A fresh Opus reader (a90c3d35ce434f40d) checked the rephrasing against his words; six wordings that said more than he did were corrected. His statement differs from the built mod in five places, recorded for stage 2 and 3: the smelter wreck cannot be picked up (c_wreck_cannot_be_carried, core); the power-cell wreck gives a faint current (c_wreck_gives_a_trickle, core); only one factory machine is onboarded (c_half_ancient_factory, core, with the draft ask a_which_factory_machines); Kludged needs no study and Refurbished lacks a recipe (build items); a Mod Setting, off as shipped, brings the Original back (one line at stage 3). Resolved: c_factory_mod_required, c_original_means_two_things. The offer of a look at the running mod (turn_01.md) has no answer from him and still stands; stage 2 carries it.

quick_look.scene: One save on the mod's small list: the smelter at its grades side by side, the power cell and the psychic emanator at theirs, and a colonist sent to study a wreck. He sees whether the grades can be told apart by eye at play zoom, and what study at a machine looks like. Neither of the two asks waits for the look.

results.summary: Stage 2, turn 2 sent (design/concepts/WreckedMachines/turn_02.md): two asks wait for him. a_which_factory_machines: how many of the factory mod's 18 production machines 0.1.0 onboards: one (the smelter, built today), all 18, or a proven handful of three; recommended the handful, judged on whether a second machine can go through onboarding by the written steps; the cost is 0, 136 or 16 new pictures. a_component_source: where an Ancient Component comes from: out of another wreck that is taken apart, a rare find in ruins, or both; recommended both. A fresh Opus judge (a15c1525ac03b2c3f) passed both asks with no rewording, measured the count of 18 again, and had three sentences of the page corrected that said more than his words. Seven calls were taken without asking, each shown to him on the page as a reading he can refuse: a wreck of any size is carried home and repaired where it stands (his newer statement decides over his 2026-09-15 sentence); a Wrecked machine has no function; study comes before each repair, with two research projects for each machine; a found machine is always Wrecked and which wrecks lie where is data a layer above can change; Wrecked, Kludged and whole are told apart by eye; the three rules outside the promise work as today until each move lands; a relic's value outside colony wealth waits for the next version. Five contradictions are resolved (c_wreck_cannot_be_carried, c_wreck_gives_a_trickle, c_study_fights_build_over, c_grades_share_one_picture, c_riders_in_the_folder). Two core contradictions stay open, each on one of the asks: c_half_ancient_factory and c_no_way_in. a_how_study_feels is struck: his statement settled it. The offer of a look at the running mod has no answer from him and is repeated.

quick_look.scene: ACCEPTED by him on 2026-11-26 (OWNER:1795760440829904733); staging is the item RIMMANDRAKE_STAGE_WRECKED_MACHINES_LOOK_HE_SAID_YES. One save on the mod's small list, six stations (design/concepts/WreckedMachines/look_01.md): the smelter at its four built grades side by side, the power cell and the psychic emanator at theirs beside the vanilla machine, a colonist sent to study a wreck, a Kludged smelter about to be built over a wreck, and a wrecked smelter beside a wrecked power cell to show what moving a wreck is today. He sees whether the grades can be told apart by eye at play zoom and what study at a machine looks like. None of the three asks waits for the look.

results.summary: Stage 2, turn 3 sent (design/concepts/WreckedMachines/turn_03.md). His reply to turn 2 (OWNER:1795760440829904733) is taken in. (1) He accepted the look at the running mod: what the save shows is written in design/concepts/WreckedMachines/look_01.md (six stations on the mod's small list), and the staging is filed as RIMMANDRAKE_STAGE_WRECKED_MACHINES_LOOK_HE_SAID_YES, because a Designer run may not take a game. (2) He said that a wreck can be moved by special hauler droids or ride-in machines, through Droidworks. That reopens one part of the turn-2 call d_wreck_is_carried: who lifts a wreck. Measured: the Property mod has a hauler job and five Droidworks chassis carry its marker; the job acts only on a building with a carried form, and the built smelter wreck has none, so today no pawn lifts it; the lift list of 2026-11-01 makes a wrecked machine 'droid only' and its pass is not built; Droidworks is a RimStarWars campaign mod, and this mod stands alone, so a stranger's game has no hauler. One new ask waits for him, a_who_moves_a_wreck: in a game without Droidworks a wrecked smelter gets home by hand (with the lift as data that the campaign narrows to haulers), by a hauler that this mod brings, or not at all; recommended by hand, judged on whether a stranger can do what the root says. A fresh Opus judge (a44e086c95b4295e7) passed the ask and had three sentences corrected that said more than their sources. The last four words of his reply ('but notified or built') are kept as typed and nothing is read from them; the Conductor asked him. The two asks of turn 2 (a_which_factory_machines, a_component_source) have no answer and stay sent. Three core contradictions are open, each on one ask: c_half_ancient_factory, c_no_way_in, c_who_lifts_a_wreck.

quick_look.why: A look cannot settle a_plasteel_on_the_forge: the alloy forge has no Wrecked or Kludged level built, so nothing that runs shows either picture. The look that he accepted on 2026-11-26 (OWNER:1795760440829904733) is already being staged on RIMMANDRAKE_STAGE_WRECKED_MACHINES_FIRST_LOOK_ONLY_ONE_BUILD_EVER_PLAYED; it explores d_three_looks and d_study_before_each_repair.

results.summary: Stage 2, turn 4 sent (design/concepts/WreckedMachines/turn_04.md). His three card answers of 2026-11-26 are taken in and cited: all 18 factory machines are ancient in 0.1.0 (OWNER:1795761534460592124); an Ancient Component is 'Only found in ruins or via plot' (OWNER:1795761550785045693); colonists carry a wreck (OWNER:1795762605668672773). The three asks are answered and three core contradictions are resolved (c_no_way_in, c_half_ancient_factory, c_who_lifts_a_wreck). Measured from the factory mod's defs: the 18 machines by name (17 without Vanilla Cooking Expanded), masses 35 to 115 kg, six supporting parts that stay buildable, no trade tag or reward tag on any of the 18. The Designer's calls, shown to him on the page: each machine leaves the build menu as the smelter does today; a machine that stands in an old save is not changed; one Mod Settings switch per machine; two research projects per machine; a component lies only in ruins, and 'via plot' is read as the campaign's story (marked as a reading); who may lift a wreck is data that the campaign narrows. One finding changes an earlier reading: the alloy forge is one of the 18, so its research step that opens it for building ends when the forge is onboarded (d_forge_is_onboarded; d_riders_fate and d_riders_move_no_interim corrected). That opens one new ask, a_plasteel_on_the_forge: plasteel from a late research project on any working forge (his sentence of 2026-10-09 and the built mod), or as the recipe of the Refurbished forge (one Ancient Component), or both; recommended the Refurbished forge, judged on whether a colony has a reason to spend a component on the forge. One core contradiction is open on that ask (c_plasteel_behind_a_component). A fresh Opus judge (a5105ca4acff55348) struck the first draft, which had decided the plasteel question as a reading and held a false cost line on durasteel; after the corrections its third read passed the ask and the page. The four words 'but notified or built' are still not read. The look that he accepted runs on the Conductor's item RIMMANDRAKE_STAGE_WRECKED_MACHINES_FIRST_LOOK_ONLY_ONE_BUILD_EVER_PLAYED and does not wait for this ask.

Stage 2 is done: no ask is open and no core contradiction is unresolved. His answer '1: b.' (OWNER:1795769070699312426) is taken in: plasteel is the recipe of the Refurbished alloy forge. He picked (b) and not (c), so the late plasteel research project and the two forge settings end with the forge's onboarding; 'Durasteel earlier, plasteel later' holds through the repair levels. Measured from the factory mod's defs: the forge has six processes, and in a game with this mod and the factory mod alone the Kludged forge makes at most obsidian (in the campaign also durasteel, after the Armoury's change). The first look at the built mod (the Conductor's findings note, BENCH event 1795766557136982102) is taken in as d_first_look_read: a shade of one picture does not tell two levels apart; a repair today is a pick from the Factory build tab, and a colonist takes the wreck apart before the frame is built; Research Reinvented's study needs a field research kit and an order for every session; the smelter wreck cannot be carried. Three calls were taken without a card, shown to him on design/concepts/WreckedMachines/turn_05.md and logged for his digest (OWNER event 1795770570858909459): (A) a repair is ordered on the machine and made on the machine, the machine stays in sight at its lower level until the work is complete, a cancelled repair never costs the colony the machine, and no level of an onboarded machine is in the build menu; (B) while a machine's Mod Settings line is on, the world hands out no working one, the base game's vanometric power cell and psychic emanator included (today the base game gives each as a reward, as exotic trader stock and as map loot: measured); (C) gravlite sits with plasteel on the Refurbished forge. Call B is the one to show him first: the Designer's first draft left the base game's cell in the world, a fresh Opus reader (aa3f32904cbb116b2) struck that on his words 'used only for comparison', the Designer reversed it, and a second reader (af92389435438039f) passed the page. It changes the base game for a stranger and he can undo it with one line. Read from the base game's source and not yet seen in play: that a cancelled repair order loses the wreck. Still owed before a bar leans on it: a look at the base game's own study on a building. One fault of the built mod is recorded for the build's first live visit (c_bolt_on_powered_machine: a no-power mark on the Refurbished smelter while it reads powered). The four words 'but notified or built' are still not read. No word of his on the 9 captures of the first look is on the ledger yet; a word from him reopens this stage. Next: stage 3 writes the sheet, the tree of bars, the plan and the scenes.

results.summary: Stage 3 closed. Run rm-role-designer-1795773471 wrote the design and died on an API 529 before its result; this run finished it. On disk: sheet.md, tree.json (12 six-part bars, whole bar whole_journey, 12 checks, 17 rules, 17 meetings), plan.md (with the offline-simulation answer: yes for the repair state machine and the onboarding table, no for the rest), scenes.json (22 acceptance, 2 interaction and 4 exploration scenes; 3 showcases, flagship smelter_comes_home by a delegated pick), floor.json, models.md and root.md. Gate A lint passes and the showcase set is accepted. This run: (1) filed the build item RIMMANDRAKE_SCRIPT_WRECKED_MACHINES_SCENES_EVERY_REPAIR_A_FOIL with its acceptance test, seen red (23 entry points missing), published at 694c69f167; (2) wrote version/next_version/README.md, the eight 'later' lines of the sheet as pre-written tickets, which opens no version; (3) ran one fresh reader (rm-judge, opus) over the whole design: all 18 quotes of the sheet are word for word in their events, and four significant faults were found and fixed here. The largest: the repair bar promised the repair of a found wreck where it stands, and the ground rule refused it on a ruin's floor. The game's source (GenConstruct.CanPlaceBlueprintOver) and the factory mod's floor def settle the rule: a wreck names no ground need, the colony lays factory floor under it or carries it onto floor, and the scene sc_repair_needs_ground must show both ways in play. The others: the whole bar's first picture now matches the one Ancient Component of its scenes; the settings scene can no longer pass on settings that never apply; rule R_lift says what a narrowing of the lift does. No bar was added and no bar's 'says' changed. Open for later stages: one meeting is unknown (study on a building; the spike is built first); his reaction to the 9 captures of the first look is not on the ledger, and a word from him reopens stage 2.
